- Captain Elias Vane logs anomalies in photographic plates, dismissed as atmospheric distortion by Admiralty board

- Okafor's paper "Civilizations Unseen: Photographic Census of the Western Hemisphere" shatters Eurocentric historiography overnight

* 1923 — First manned orbital vessel Krasnyi Oreh crash-lands within Amazon basin; crew of four survives, trades with Kichwa Confederacy
- Linguist Anya Petrova spends eleven years documenting Kichwa, producing the definitive grammar that becomes the Rosetta Stone for all subsequent contact

* 1931 — The Green Continent is formally mapped via triangulated satellite passes; population estimates revised to four billion
- League of Nations establishes the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs in Geneva; first diplomatic envoys arrive at Aztec capital Tenochtitlán

* 1938 — Total war erupts between Kichwa Confederacy and Aztec Empire over disputed Orinoco territory; both deploy orbital bombardment
- The "Shattering" kills an estimated two hundred million; orbital debris creates a permanent twilight band over the equator

* 1945 — After the Shattering, surviving Western Continent civilizations issue the "Treaty of Silence," banning all further orbital access by Old World powers
- The satellite program is dismantled; last orbital station "Prometheus" deliberately deorbited over the Pacific

* 1967 — Cold War tensions reignite when a stolen Russian satellite fragment reveals the Western Continent never truly went silent — underground cities pulse with bioluminescent light
- The "Revealed Age" begins; humanity's entire understanding of itself fractures into irreparable pieces
